how_md:
**How to use (Comprehensible Input):**
- Pick the **easiest tier where you understand about 70–80% with English subtitles**. Too hard = noise, not learning.
- **Focused listening** (eyes on screen, subtitles on) counts most. **Background listening** while walking, waiting or working is a bonus — best with things you've already watched once.
- **Re-watch** favourites. The 2nd and 3rd time is where your ears catch up with your eyes.
- Don't pause for every word. Follow the story or idea.
- Log your minutes in the lesson feedback box ("Extra English today"). Tell your tutor which ones you like — the library will grow around them.

tiers.name: Tier 1 · Easy – start here
tiers.note: Made for learners: slower speech, clear voices, often with transcripts. Your main daily listening now.

items.name: 6 Minute English – BBC Learning English
items.why: 6-minute episodes, two hosts, **free transcripts**. Perfect for listen → read → listen again.

items.name: VOA Learning English
items.why: Real news read **slowly** with a limited vocabulary; text on the same page.

items.name: Easy English
items.why: Real people, natural speech, **subtitles on screen**. Great for getting used to real voices.

items.name: All Ears English
items.why: Friendly American conversation, around B1–B2. Good for background listening.

items.name: Speak English With Vanessa
items.why: Clear, slightly slow American English; lots of natural everyday phrases.

tiers.name: Tier 2 · Your interests – with subtitles
tiers.note: Real content for native viewers, short and visual. Use English subtitles; watch twice.

items.name: TED-Ed
items.why: 5-minute animated lessons; the pictures carry the meaning when a sentence is hard.

items.name: Psych2Go
items.why: Simple language, short videos, topic you like.

items.name: CNBC Make It
items.why: Short real-life stories; clear documentary-style narration.

items.name: Luke's English Podcast
items.why: Long, chatty episodes by an English teacher – great for long walks once Tier 1 feels easy.

items.name: Learn English With TV Series
items.why: Real scenes, then explained – a bridge to watching shows.

items.name: Binging with Babish
items.why: Cooking from films/series; you can follow by watching even when speech is fast.

items.name: Joshua Weissman
items.why: Energetic cooking videos; fast but very visual.

tiers.name: Tier 3 · Stretch – try, don't force
tiers.note: Faster, denser. Try one when Tier 2 feels comfortable; if you understand <60%, go back a tier.

items.name: AI Explained
items.why: Careful explanations of new AI models – your favourite topic.

items.name: Two Minute Papers
items.why: Short; lots of visuals. Accent takes getting used to.

items.name: ColdFusion
items.why: Calm narration, documentary style.

items.name: Kurzgesagt – In a Nutshell
items.why: Beautiful animation; fast and dense – re-watch.

items.name: Hard Fork (New York Times)
items.why: Two journalists chatting about tech every week. Native speed – a great long-term goal.

items.name: Veritasium
items.why: Clear storytelling, longer videos.

items.name: Vox
items.why: Strong visuals, fast narration.

items.name: TED
items.why: Talks have interactive transcripts; choose speakers with slow, clear delivery.
